question: A spinal curve measuring 8° by the Cobb method is classified as scoliosis and requires bracing to prevent progression.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. The Cobb angle threshold for diagnosing scoliosis is ≥10°. An 8° curve does not meet the definition and does not require bracing. Bracing is generally initiated for progressive curves in the 25–40° range in skeletally immature patients.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Incorrect. A curve of 8° is below the diagnostic threshold. Scoliosis is defined as a lateral spinal curvature of ≥10° by Cobb angle. Curves of <10° are within normal limits; bracing is not indicated.
